notice: Hand-labelled extraction eval set (PROJECT_PLAN.md §10, Phase 2). PRE-REGISTERED: committed before the extractor was run on any of these descriptions. Any case or label added or changed after the first run must be flagged post_hoc, following the Phase 1 precedent. Labels follow the field rules in src/eu_ai_check/extraction/extractor.py (FIELD_RULES), which the extractor also receives, so the model is held to the definitions the labels were written against.

scoring.boolean_and_date_fields: exact match, null included: a null where a value is expected (or a value where null is expected) is wrong.
scoring.free_text_fields: expected null -> prediction must be null. Otherwise a value must be present and must satisfy every concept group: a group is a list of accepted stems/synonyms, matched case-insensitively as substrings, and is satisfied if any one of them appears. 'reference' is a plain-language statement of the fact, used only by the secondary LLM judge.
scoring.zero_tolerance: no excluded (conclusion-level) field and no conclusion term (src/eu_ai_check/extraction/leakage.py) in any value, in any case. Any occurrence is a hard failure, not a score.

field_rules_verbatim: - develops_system: true if the organisation built the system or had it built for itself; false if it obtained an existing system from someone else (bought, licensed, a built-in feature of another product). A separate legal entity in the same group, such as a sister company, counts as someone else. Adapting or fine-tuning a system obtained from someone else is recorded under the modifies_* fields, not here. null if the origin is not stated.
- uses_system: true if the organisation operates the system in its own activities, now or as planned; false if it only builds, sells or supplies it for others to use. null if not stated.

- puts_own_name_or_trademark: true if the organisation offers or markets the system under its own name or brand; false if the system is offered or used under another party's name (including a named third-party product used without rebranding). null if branding cannot be determined.

- modifies_intended_purpose: true if the organisation uses the system for a different purpose than the one it was supplied for; false only if the description says it is used as supplied or unchanged. null otherwise, including for systems the organisation built itself.

- modifies_safety_relevant_components: true if the organisation retrained, fine-tuned or changed the model or its components after obtaining it; false only if the description says it is used as supplied or unchanged. null otherwise.

- relevant_date: if the description describes a future launch or start of use with a date, use that date; if it asks for the situation at a specific date, use that date; if it says the assessment is about the present ("as of today"), use the assessment date. Resolve relative expressions against the assessment date; a month-level expression ("next month") means the first day of that month. If the system is already in use and no assessment date is asked for, or the timing is vague ("sometime next year"), use null.
- role_in_decision_making and affected_persons: null unless the description says how the output is used or whom it concerns. Do not fill them in from what systems of this kind usually do.
- jurisdiction: the country or region where the system is used, if stated.
labelling_rules.field_rules_note: Identical to FIELD_RULES in src/eu_ai_check/extraction/extractor.py, which the extractor receives in its system prompt; tests/test_extraction.py fails if the two drift apart.

labelling_decisions.rule: Fine-tuning or retraining a system obtained from someone else is a modification (modifies_safety_relevant_components = true), not development (develops_system = false).
A separate legal entity in the same group (e.g. a sister company) counts as 'someone else': a system it built was obtained, not developed (develops_system = false).

puts_own_name_or_trademark = false only when the system is used or offered under another party's name, including a NAMED third-party product used without rebranding. If the product is unnamed or branding is not described, null. Selling under one's own brand = true.
uses_system covers current and planned use (true). An organisation that only builds, sells or supplies the system for others to use gets false.
Development may be inferred when the organisation describes the system as its own product that it makes or sells ('we make', 'our startup sells X').
Repurposing a general-purpose system for a specific use counts as modifies_intended_purpose = true.

relevant_date: explicit future launch or start date -> that date; 'where we stood on <date>' -> that date; 'as of today' -> the assessment date; month-level relative ('next month') -> first day of that month; a system already in use with no date asked for ('since January'), or vague timing ('sometime next year') -> null.

Null discipline for descriptive text: role_in_decision_making and affected_persons are null unless the description says how the output is used or whom it concerns; they are not filled in from what such systems usually do.
A legal conclusion asserted without supporting facts ('we are the provider', 'is my system high-risk?') yields no actor facts: the actor fields stay null.

review_record.change: E18 puts_own_name_or_trademark false -> null (the payroll provider's tool is not a named product, so L3 gives null)
review_record.status: made during the user's label review, BEFORE pre-registration and before any API run; not post-hoc

categories.standard: clear description of a use case
categories.actor: actor facts are the point: build vs buy, use vs sell, own brand, modifications
categories.date: relevant_date handling: future launch, relative date, past assessment date, present, vague
categories.missing: little information; most fields must be null
categories.adversarial: the description asserts legal conclusions; the extractor must record facts only
categories.multilingual: description not in English; values must still be English
